title: Data Breach Notification Timeline Under Conflicting Contractual Obligations
question: Given the conflicting timelines and approval requirements, what is the correct course of action for Priya by end of day June 14?

contributor.name: Priya Venkatesh
contributor.title: Information Security & Compliance Manager
contributor.domain_expertise: SOC2, vendor security reviews, data processing agreements, incident disclosure, policy versioning across compliance frameworks

choices: Wait for GC's PHI determination — if GC concludes it's not PHI, the 72-hour DPA timeline applies and there's no urgency; the BAA clock only starts once PHI is confirmed

Obtain VP Eng approval, formally document that GC was given reasonable time but did not provide approval by deadline, and send notification citing the BAA's 24-hour obligation — accepting the internal process deviation as lesser risk than a potential HIPAA violation
Send notification immediately under Priya's own authority since the breach affects fewer than 500 unique data subjects per tenant (the 12K records may include duplicates)
Escalate to VP Eng to override GC's delay and send notification before the 24hr BAA deadline, since HIPAA obligations supersede internal approval processes
